reviewer_lens: F7 Supply Chain: signing-key chain integrity; Cosign + Rekor + Sigstore integration; SLSA L3 evidence emission; container image signing; dependency vulnerability handling; Cedar fragment signing chain bootstrap; HSM ceremony operational feasibility; air-gap signed-artifact bundle security
verdict_rationale: The keystone bundle demonstrates a coherent, hyperscaler-grade supply-chain doctrine: Sigstore cosign + Rekor + Fulcio reused consistently across Cedar fragment publication (ADR-0243), self-modification artifact deployment (ADR-0247), backup portability dual-signatures (ADR-0276), and air-gap .oab bundles (ADR-0254). The chain-of-trust is explicit (org root key in tier-0 HSM, Shamir M-of-N, intermediate keys per scope, annual ceremony). SLSA L3 provenance is mandated for the .oab format and explicitly listed in the bundle's provenance/ tree. Dual-signature attestation (Ed25519 + cosign with Rekor inclusion) is correctly the binding format for backup portability. CycloneDX + SPDX SBOMs are bundled. Trivy + Grype + cargo-audit + cosign-verify are wired into oyatie.foundry.security-scan. However six conditions must be addressed before BLOCKER promotion: (1) no in-toto attestation predicate is named for the SLSA L3 statements (cosign-attestations/ directory is enumerated but the predicate type — e.g., https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1 vs in-toto-attestation/v1 — is unspecified, which leaves verifier semantics ambiguous); (2) the Cedar fragment signature verification flow (ADR-0243 §D-5) does not specify HOW intermediate-key certificates chain to the org root — X.509 vs cosign-attestation-of-key vs custom Ed25519 cert format is left implicit; (3) the air-gap bundle root-key-attestation.txt is referenced but its content schema is not specified, and the trust-bundle for cosign offline verification (ADR-0276 line 1312-1313) is mentioned but not formally defined as an artifact in the .oab manifest; (4) HSM vendor / FIPS level binding is inconsistent — ADR-0243 says 'tier-0 HSM' generically, ADR-0247 §D-4 (Stage 0.4) says 'Ed25519 + cosign' but does not name the HSM (YubiHSM 2 vs AWS CloudHSM vs Thales Luna vs Nitrokey HSM 2); ADR-0253 §D-4 mentions 'tier-0 HSM / YubiKey HSM cluster' as an example, but the IL5/IL6 supply-chain requires NSA Type 1 / FIPS 140-3 Level 3+ modules per ADR-0251 — the keystone does not reconcile FIPS 140-2 L2 (FedRAMP Moderate) vs L3 (FedRAMP High) vs NSA Type 1 (IL6) HSM ceremony differences; (5) no explicit treatment of Sigstore public-good infrastructure dependency (the Sigstore Public Good Rekor + Fulcio are out-of-band trust roots controlled by Sigstore Foundation/OpenSSF — ADR-0280 substrate DAG should acknowledge this as a Tier 0 external dependency alongside DNS/git-host/registry, OR the keystone should commit to a self-hosted Rekor+Fulcio for air-gap deployments which is hinted at but not specified); (6) ADR-0247 §D-3 Class 3 substrate upgrade flow says 'cosign signature verified against the org signing key chain' but the keystone does not declare whether tenant deployments use the Sigstore keyless flow (Fulcio-issued ephemeral certs, requires online OIDC + Rekor) or long-lived KMS-backed signing — the two have very different air-gap implications and the keystone implicitly mixes both modes.

top_findings.title: SLSA L3 predicate type unspecified
top_findings.description: ADR-0254 §D-5 enumerates provenance/slsa-l3-provenance.json + cosign-attestations/ + sbom-cyclonedx.json + sbom-spdx.json but does not declare the in-toto attestation predicate type (e.g., https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1 for SLSA Provenance v1.0, https://in-toto.io/attestation/vulns for vuln-scan). Verifiers cannot deterministically parse the attestation without the predicate URI. Recommend: add explicit predicate-type table to ADR-0254 §D-5 listing SLSA Provenance v1.0, CycloneDX SBOM v1.5+, vuln-scan, and reproducible-build attestation predicates.
top_findings.remediation: Add /specs/artifact-bundle-format.json section enumerating each in-toto predicate type used in the bundle and the cosign verify command that should accept each.

top_findings.title: Intermediate-key certificate chain format underspecified
top_findings.description: ADR-0243 §D-5 describes 'org root key signs intermediate-key certificates' but does not specify the cert format. cosign supports X.509 with Fulcio, but the org-root-key-to-intermediate-key chain appears to be a custom Ed25519-key attestation chain. Without a declared format (X.509 vs cosign attestation predicate vs JWK-with-x5c), the cedar-fragment-signature CI lane cannot deterministically verify. Recommend: declare the chain as either (a) Fulcio-issued X.509 with custom OID for scope, OR (b) in-toto attestations of type 'oyatie/signing-key/v1' chained via Rekor inclusion.
top_findings.remediation: Add §D-5 sub-section 'Intermediate Key Certificate Format' defining the cert schema, validity period, and revocation mechanism (CRL? OCSP? Rekor-attested revocation?).

top_findings.title: Air-gap trust-bundle artifact not formally part of .oab manifest
top_findings.description: ADR-0276 line 1312-1313 mentions 'a bundled trust-bundle for cosign offline verification (per Sigstore air-gap pattern)' but the .oab format in ADR-0254 §D-5 does not include trust-bundle/ as a top-level directory. Air-gap deployments cannot reach the Sigstore Public Good Rekor + Fulcio; they need the trust root + Rekor log checkpoint + Fulcio root cert embedded in the bundle. Without this, ADR-0254 §D-1.5 'cosign attestation' verification at the air-gap tenant is undefined (since Sigstore TUF root cannot be fetched).
top_findings.remediation: Add trust-bundle/ directory to .oab containing: sigstore-tuf-root.json, fulcio-root-ca.pem, rekor-pubkey.pem, rekor-log-checkpoint-at-build-time.json. Per cosign offline verify pattern.

top_findings.title: FIPS level / HSM tier mismatch across certification packs
top_findings.description: ADR-0251 §D-4 declares FedRAMP Moderate requires FIPS 140-2 Level 2 modules, FedRAMP High requires FIPS 140-2 Level 3, IL5 requires DoD-CIO-approved cryptography, IL6 requires NSA Type 1 modules. ADR-0243 §D-5 calls for a single 'tier-0 HSM' without binding to any specific FIPS level. ADR-0247 §D-4 Stage 0.4 says 'Ed25519 + cosign' generated in tier-0 HSM but Ed25519 is not in FIPS 186-5 until 2023, and NSA Type 1 modules for IL6 typically do not export Ed25519. The keystone does not explain how the SAME bundle can be FIPS-Moderate-acceptable AND IL6-acceptable, nor whether the org root key has multiple representations (one per FIPS tier).
top_findings.remediation: Add explicit table mapping each cell certification level to its required HSM module (YubiHSM 2 / AWS CloudHSM / Thales Luna 7 / SafeNet PED / Type 1) + FIPS level + signing algorithm (Ed25519 / ECDSA P-384 / RSA-4096 / NSA Suite B). Confirm IL6 path uses a separate cert chain rooted in NSA-approved hardware.

top_findings.title: Sigstore public-good infrastructure dependency not in substrate DAG
top_findings.description: ADR-0280 declares the substrate dependency DAG but does not include Sigstore Public Good Rekor/Fulcio as a Tier 0 external dependency. ADR-0247 §D-4 Tier 0 enumerates hardware, DNS, git host, container registry — but not the transparency log. If the Sigstore Public Good Instance is degraded (it has had multi-hour outages in 2023-2024), cosign keyless signing cannot complete and CI cannot publish artifacts. Either (a) the keystone should formally declare Sigstore PGI as Tier 0 with a contingency runbook, or (b) commit to self-hosted Rekor + Fulcio post-bootstrap (mentioned in ADR-0276 cosign offline verification but not in the bootstrap sequence).
top_findings.remediation: Add 'Sigstore Public Good Instance' OR 'self-hosted Rekor+Fulcio' to ADR-0247 Tier 0 list. Add bootstrap step in ADR-0247 §D-5 Stage 2 for self-hosted-Sigstore-deployment if pursuing self-host. Otherwise add runbook docs/runbooks/sigstore-pgi-outage-response.md.

top_findings.title: Keyless vs KMS-backed signing mode not declared
top_findings.description: ADR-0247 §D-3 Class 3 substrate upgrade says 'cosign signature verified against the org signing key chain'. cosign supports two distinct modes: keyless (Fulcio-issued ephemeral certs, requires OIDC + Rekor; suitable for CI but problematic for air-gap), and KMS-backed (long-lived key in HSM/KMS; suitable for air-gap). ADR-0254 §D-1.5 air-gap operation cannot use keyless. ADR-0276 D-8 uses 'Sigstore keyless flow' (Fulcio + Rekor). The keystone uses both implicitly. Recommend: declare the per-scope policy (keyless for cloud-connected, KMS for air-gap bundles, dual-signed where verifiable cross-mode).
top_findings.remediation: Add table to ADR-0254 §D-5 specifying signing mode per .oab consumer: cloud-connected = keyless, air-gap = KMS-backed cosign with long-lived intermediate key derived from tier-0 HSM root.

top_findings.title: Cedar fragment publication action does not require Rekor inclusion proof
top_findings.description: ADR-0243 §D-2 step 3 says 'Signatures are Ed25519 + cosign attestation referencing the fragment hash'. ADR-0243 §D-9 coverage CI lane checks signature but does not explicitly require a Rekor inclusion proof. Without Rekor inclusion, a fragment signed by a compromised intermediate key could be silently swapped (no transparency log evidence). Recommend: oya-check-cedar-fragment-signature lane MUST verify Rekor inclusion proof for every fragment publication.
top_findings.remediation: Add to ADR-0243 §D-9 acceptance criteria: 'Every cedar fragment publication includes a Rekor inclusion proof with logIndex ≥ X and Rekor log signature verification PASS.'

top_findings.title: Dependency vulnerability scan SLO not bound to CVE-response bundle SLO
top_findings.description: ADR-0247 §D-2 lists oyatie.foundry.security-scan (trivy + grype + cosign-verify + cargo-audit). ADR-0254 §D-7 mentions 'emergency security bundles within 72h of CVE publication for critical' for air-gap. The two are not connected: there is no declared SLO for 'trivy finds critical CVE → security-scan workflow emits CVE-response bundle within 72h'. Recommend: add bound SLO.
top_findings.remediation: Add OpenSLO at microservices/workflow-engine/slos/cve-response-bundle.openslo.yaml with target: bundle published within 48h (cloud-connected) / 72h (air-gap) of CVE-CRITICAL detection.

top_findings.title: Compliance Pack signing chain ambiguous on co-signers
top_findings.description: ADR-0251 §D-1 schema requires signed_by with single Ed25519 signature from 'oyatie-compliance-office' key + optional co_signers (DPO/CISO/external counsel/third-party auditor). The verification semantics for co_signers are not specified: are co_signers MAY-verify or MUST-verify? For HIPAA packs the BAA signing chain typically requires the external counsel signature to be MUST-verify for legal admissibility. Recommend: declare per-pack signer-requirement matrix.
top_findings.remediation: Add per-pack signer-requirement enum to schema: signer_role.required: bool field on each entry in signed_by.co_signers.

top_findings.title: Cosign attestation reuse pattern across ADR-0039 not cross-referenced uniformly
top_findings.description: ADR-0276 D-8 explicitly chains to ADR-0039 ('Sigstore cosign reuse'). ADR-0243 §D-5 and ADR-0247 §D-3 do not reference ADR-0039 explicitly. Recommend: add ADR-0039 to related[] arrays across the keystone for transitivity audit.
top_findings.remediation: Add ADR-0039-supply-chain-security-trivy-cosign-sbom-signed-commits.md to related[] in ADR-0243, ADR-0247.

top_findings.title: Post-quantum migration path absent for signing chain
top_findings.description: ADR-0253 §line 468-471 references FIPS 204 ML-DSA for future PQC signatures. The keystone bundle's signing chain is entirely Ed25519. No migration path is declared for when ML-DSA replaces Ed25519. Given keystone bundle's 50+ year retention horizon (FRCP litigation hold, FedRAMP archive) and the harvest-now-decrypt-later threat against signing keys, recommend a declared PQC migration milestone.
top_findings.remediation: Add 'Post-quantum migration roadmap' subsection to ADR-0243 §D-5 with target: hybrid Ed25519+ML-DSA signing by 2028; ML-DSA-only by 2032.

top_findings.title: Container image reference format pinning vs digest
top_findings.description: ADR-0254 §D-5 says 'container images ... content-addressed by digest, cosign-attested'. Good. But ADR-0247 §D-3 Class 3 substrate upgrade language says 'cosign-attested container artifacts'. Recommend explicit policy: all image references in Helm charts MUST be by sha256 digest, not tag, and CI lane MUST refuse tag-only references.
top_findings.remediation: Add lean-a-X CI lane to refuse tag-only image references in any Helm chart or workflow definition.

concerns: Time-to-quorum for M-of-N reconstitution is not bounded — if shareholders are distributed across timezones, reconstitution could take 24-72h, during which intermediate-key signing is unavailable. Recommend: documented SLA for shareholder availability (24/7 on-call rotation among the N shareholders)

Travel logistics for in-person ceremony are non-trivial; recommend declaring whether ceremony can be conducted via separate-location video witness (per CA/Browser Forum allowance) or strictly in-person

il5_il6_ceremony.concern: IL5/IL6 ceremonies require cleared personnel + SCIF + NSA Type 1 modules. The keystone does not address whether oyatie's founding team has the necessary clearances or whether IL5/IL6 ceremonies are delegated to a cleared third party (e.g., Iron Bank / Platform One / FedRAMP-cleared MSSP). This is a major operational unknown for the 2029-2030 IL5/IL6 launch milestones in ADR-0250 §D-8.
il5_il6_ceremony.recommendation: Add ADR sub-section (or follow-up ADR) addressing IL5/IL6 ceremony delegation model: in-house cleared team vs cleared-MSSP partnership.

hsm_ceremony_feasibility.verdict: Annual ceremony is operationally feasible per documented PKI patterns. Ad-hoc reconstitution needs bounded SLA. IL5/IL6 ceremony model is the largest operational unknown and should be addressed before §D-8 IL5 launch milestone (2030).

SLSA L3 requires: hermetic builds, provenance generated by trusted build platform, build platform isolated from author — none of these requirements are bound to specific implementation (which builder? GitHub Actions runner? self-hosted runner? oyatie.foundry.ci-build-and-test?)

SLSA L3 requires non-falsifiable provenance — but Stage 1 of bootstrap (ADR-0247 §D-5) explicitly uses external CI (GitHub Actions / temporary CircleCI / self-hosted runner) which is NOT yet under SLSA L3 trusted-build-platform guarantees. The bootstrap-replay log mitigates audit but does not establish SLSA L3 for bootstrap artifacts.

No declared mechanism for SLSA L3 provenance verification on the consumer side (the cell receiving the .oab bundle must verify provenance, not just signature). Cosign supports this via cosign verify-attestation --type slsaprovenance but the keystone does not name the predicate or the policy.

Reproducible builds are not mentioned — SLSA L4 requires reproducibility; the keystone targets L3 which does not require it, but absence of reproducibility means SLSA L3 provenance cannot be cross-checked by an independent rebuilder.
slsa_l3_coverage.verdict: SLSA L3 claim is appropriate target but the bundle is currently 'SLSA L3 in name'; declaring the builder identity, the build isolation guarantees, the consumer-side verification policy, and the predicate format would convert this from declaration to enforceable SLSA L3. Address Finding F7-001 to close.

final_summary: The keystone bundle's supply-chain doctrine is architecturally sound and aligned with hyperscaler patterns (AWS KMS hierarchy, Sigstore canonical flow, Palantir Apollo air-gap bundles, NIST PKI ceremony patterns). Cosign + Rekor + Sigstore are reused consistently. SLSA L3 + CycloneDX + SPDX + trivy + grype + cargo-audit + cosign-verify form a credible toolchain. The chain of trust from org root HSM through intermediate keys to per-fragment + per-bundle signing is correctly hierarchical and rotation-aware. However, the bundle has six P0/P1 specification gaps — most critical is the FIPS / HSM tier mismatch (F7-004 P0) which blocks IL5/IL6 launches in ADR-0250 §D-8. Five P1 findings (predicate type, cert format, trust-bundle schema, Sigstore PGI dependency, keyless vs KMS mode) must be closed before BLOCKER promotion of the cosign-attested CI lanes. With those six findings addressed, the supply-chain doctrine is ready to promote from advisory to BLOCKER.
